title: Frontend: sum()
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind sum(). This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Implement solution(groups). Build a reusable curried accumulator that accepts each numeric argument group and is terminated by an empty call. Return the final sum. An empty groups list returns zero.
constraints: Define solution(input) in plain JavaScript. Return the documented JSON-compatible value or throw the documented validation error. Each case receives a fresh input.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
Return a function that captures the current total.
alternativeApproaches: Support grouped arguments while keeping termination unambiguous and avoiding mutation shared by sibling chains.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: sum(1)(2)(); empty termination; zero.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
